scenarios.title: Preview requested and available work
scenarios.summary: Prepare two independent lists as intact text in a comparison card.
scenarios.objective: Two arguments name existing requested-work and available-work files; REVIEWER is supplied. Print Reviewer: NAME, then Requested: <VALUE>, then Available: <VALUE>, with a line break after each. Each VALUE contains that file's lines in the ordering used by sort -u, with repeated lines listed once. Remove line breaks at the end of the command result. teaching.prerequisite_note: Use quoted arguments and sort -u from the text lessons. A command can print a value that the next part of a script needs.

concepts.title: Turn printed output into a value
concepts.text: Command substitution, written $(command), runs a command and gives you its normal printed output as a value. labels=$(sort -u loans.txt) creates labels from that output. The file name is an input to sort; it is not the value stored in labels.

concepts.title: Keep the value together
concepts.text: Use double quotes when printing the stored value: printf '<%s>\n' "$labels". Otherwise spaces and line breaks can divide it into arguments, and wildcard text such as *.txt can select virtual filenames. The quoted value stays text.

concepts.title: Understand the end of the output
concepts.text: Capture removes line breaks at the end of command output. It keeps spaces and line breaks inside the value. sort normally finishes its last row with a line break; the closing > therefore follows the last captured row. Later lessons explore several final line breaks and command status.

scenarios.title: Keep the evidence intact in a report
scenarios.summary: Normalize only the ending line breaks while preserving the note and protecting existing work.
scenarios.objective: Argument 1 names a note file; argument 2 is the report destination; REPORT_TITLE is supplied. Replace only the destination with Report: TITLE, Evidence: <VALUE>, and End report, with a line break after each. VALUE is the original note with all line breaks at its end removed; preserve every other character, including spaces, tabs and backslashes, and keep line breaks at the start and inside. Shell-looking text stays literal. Empty/all-line-break notes give <>. Print Saved: DEST plus a line break; return 0 with no error output. teaching.prerequisite_note: Use capture from the comparison card and validation/redirection from the report lessons. This task preserves the note itself, rather than sorting its lines.

concepts.title: Remove ending line breaks, keep the evidence
concepts.text: $(cat "$source") reads command output into a value. Capture removes every line break at the end. It keeps line breaks at the start and inside, spaces, tabs and other text. An empty or all-line-break note becomes an empty value.

concepts.title: Quoting preserves what remains
concepts.text: Double quotes preserve the captured value, including an empty value. They cannot bring back ending line breaks that capture removed. Characters such as *, %, backslashes and $(...) printed by cat are data; the output is not executed again.

concepts.title: Print the report deliberately
concepts.text: Use %s for text values and explicit \n for the report's own line breaks. printf 'Evidence: <%s>\n' "$note" places > immediately after the remaining evidence. The optional input comparison makes invisible spaces and line breaks visible.

concepts.title: Recognize invisible characters
concepts.text: Here a line break means the newline character written \n in scripts and feedback. A tab is written \t. A carriage return, written \r, is another character and stays in captured text. These differences can appear in the input and output comparison.

concepts.title: Check before replacing a file
concepts.text: Validate the destination and source before using >. A missing source must preserve an existing report. The task lists the exact checks and error messages; opening an output file too early can destroy useful work.

teaching.inputs: No arguments, files or supplied variables. printf creates the display note; note is created by the example. The two ending line breaks are removed by capture, while the blank line inside stays.

scenarios.retry_guidance: If only trailing-blank-line cases fail, distinguish the command result from its captured value. If spaces or literal patterns change, inspect quoting. A rejected input must preserve the previous report byte for byte.
scenarios.explanation: Command capture removes ending LF line-break bytes only. Quoting preserves the remaining value, including leading/interior breaks, edge spaces, tabs and a final CR character. It does not execute shell-looking data. Preflight protects useful source/report files before any output redirection.

scenarios.title: Investigate findings without losing their status
scenarios.summary: Keep a helper's value, diagnostics and decision status separate.
scenarios.objective: One argument names an inspection source. The supplied inspect_source helper prints Inspecting: NAME on error output, returns 0 and prints all lines containing literal BLOCK: when matches exist, returns 1 for no matches, or explicitly checks a missing source and prints Missing source: NAME with return 2. For an existing source print Source: NAME, Decision: hold or ready, then Findings: <VALUE>, each followed by a line break. A match means hold/status 1; no matches (including an empty file) means ready/status 0 and <>. VALUE is the complete matching-line output with line breaks at its end removed, preserving remaining text. A missing source has only the two helper error-output lines, status 2 and no normal report. Leave every file unchanged. The helper is editable; equivalent supported behavior passes. Use the supplied filenames exactly.

initial.source:
inspect_source() {
    printf 'Inspecting: %s\n' "$1" >&2
    if [ -f "$1" ]; then
        :
    else
        printf 'Missing source: %s\n' "$1" >&2
        return 2
    fi
    grep -F 'BLOCK:' "$1"
}
findings=$(inspect_source "$1")
printf 'Source: %s\n' "$1"
if [ "$?" -eq 0 ]; then
    printf 'Decision: hold\nFindings: <%s>\n' "$findings"
    exit 1
fi
printf 'Decision: ready\nFindings: <>\n'
exit 0

teaching.prerequisite_note: Use helper functions, return and separate error output. A captured value and the command's status answer different questions.

concepts.title: Capture output and check status separately
concepts.text: An assignment such as reply=$(suggest_route) stores normal output. Its status is the captured command's status. Save it immediately with route_status=$?, or put the assignment in an if condition. A later printf has its own status and replaces $?; the stored reply does not tell you that status.

concepts.title: A nonzero result can carry useful information
concepts.text: The practice helper returns 4 and still prints a useful route. The assignment helper returns 0 for matching BLOCK: lines, 1 for no matches and 2 for its explicit missing-source check. Those are ordinary supported helper results, not simulator failures. Unsupported commands, limits and Stop are different: they leave the run ungraded.

concepts.title: Normal output and diagnostics stay separate
concepts.text: Capture collects normal output only. A helper's >&2 messages still appear in the error-output view. Keep those diagnostics separate from the Findings value. In this assignment, a hold is a useful report with status 1; a missing source has diagnostics and status 2, with no normal report.

concepts.title: Make a decision before reporting it
concepts.text: The starter prints Source before inspecting $?, so it inspects printf's status instead of the helper's. A successful helper is not automatically a ready decision: this helper uses 0 to mean that blocking text was found. Follow the stated mapping rather than guessing from an empty or nonempty value.

teaching.example:
suggest_route() {
    printf 'Map: north  gate\n'
    printf 'Advice: manual check\n' >&2
    return 4
}
reply=$(suggest_route)
route_status=$?
printf 'Reply: <%s>\nStatus: %s\n' "$reply" "$route_status"
teaching.inputs: No arguments, files or supplied variables. The example defines a small helper, captures its reply, and creates route_status. The outer printf succeeds even when the helper returned 4.
teaching.try_change: Change return 4 to return 0 in suggest_route and Run. The text and diagnostic should stay the same while the displayed helper status changes.

scenarios.retry_guidance: If clear sources are held, check whether you saved the helper status before printf. If a missing source becomes ready, distinguish status 2 from the ordinary no-match status 1.
scenarios.explanation: The assignment-only command gets the captured helper's status. A later printf replaces $?, so the decision needs a saved status or immediate condition. The helper explicitly checks a missing source and returns 2; it does not rely on recovering a simulator failure. Nonzero hold/no-match statuses are useful results, while unsupported/limit/Stopped outcomes remain ungraded.

scenarios.title: Preview or publish a batch investigation safely
scenarios.summary: Combine intact captured output, reliable status, isolated variables and shared inspection files.
scenarios.objective:
Arguments are mode (preview or save), destination, then one or more source files; REPORT_TITLE is supplied. Build a report headed Review: TITLE and Decision: ready or hold. For each source argument, print Source: NAME followed by all lines containing literal BLOCK:, in argument order. Finish every report line with a line break. Any match means hold/status 1; otherwise ready/status 0. Keep the original title, literal text and repeated source arguments.

Append Checked: NAME and a line break to scan-ledger.txt for each source, keeping its existing text. Preview prints the report and preserves the destination; it still updates the ledger. Save replaces only the destination and prints Saved: DEST then Decision: VALUE, each on its own line. Leave every other file unchanged.

Check everything before any changes. Fewer than three arguments, unknown mode or empty destination gives Usage: preview|save DEST SOURCE... on error output. Next, destination scan-ledger.txt gives Unsafe destination. Then check sources in order: empty name gives Empty source name; destination collision gives Unsafe destination; scan-ledger.txt as source gives Unsafe source; missing source gives Missing source: NAME. Every guard failure prints only the stated message on error output, ends it with a line break, returns 2 and leaves all files unchanged. Use the supplied filenames exactly.

initial.source:
review_batch() {
    REPORT_TITLE='Working scan'
    blocked=0
    for source in "$@"; do
        printf 'Checked: %s\n' "$source" >> scan-ledger.txt
        printf 'Source: %s\n' "$source"
        if grep -F 'BLOCK:' "$source"; then blocked=1; fi
    done
    return "$blocked"
}

# Validate the whole batch before calling this helper.
# Then create the requested preview or saved report using the original title.

solution:
review_batch() {
    REPORT_TITLE='Working scan'
    blocked=0
    for source in "$@"; do
        printf 'Checked: %s\n' "$source" >> scan-ledger.txt
        printf 'Source: %s\n' "$source"
        if grep -F 'BLOCK:' "$source"; then blocked=1; fi
    done
    return "$blocked"
}
if [ "$#" -lt 3 ]; then
    printf 'Usage: preview|save DEST SOURCE...\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi
mode=$1
destination=$2
shift 2
if [ "$mode" != preview ] && [ "$mode" != save ]; then
    printf 'Usage: preview|save DEST SOURCE...\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi
if [ -z "$destination" ]; then
    printf 'Usage: preview|save DEST SOURCE...\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi
if [ "$destination" = scan-ledger.txt ]; then
    printf 'Unsafe destination\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi
for source in "$@"; do
    if [ -z "$source" ]; then
        printf 'Empty source name\n' >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    if [ "$source" = "$destination" ]; then
        printf 'Unsafe destination\n' >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    if [ "$source" = scan-ledger.txt ]; then
        printf 'Unsafe source\n' >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    if [ -f "$source" ]; then
        :
    else
        printf 'Missing source: %s\n' "$source" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
done
body=$(review_batch "$@")
result=$?
if [ "$result" -eq 0 ]; then decision=ready; else decision=hold; fi
if [ "$mode" = preview ]; then
    printf 'Review: %s\nDecision: %s\n%s\n' "$REPORT_TITLE" "$decision" "$body"
else
    printf 'Review: %s\nDecision: %s\n%s\n' "$REPORT_TITLE" "$decision" "$body" > "$destination"
    printf 'Saved: %s\nDecision: %s\n' "$destination" "$decision"
fi
exit "$result"

teaching.prerequisite_note: Combine the first three capture tasks with safe batches and function scope. No arrays or arithmetic are required.

concepts.title: A called helper runs inside the capture
concepts.text: A function defined earlier is available inside $(helper arguments). Capture uses an isolated shell environment: the helper sees the caller's values, but its ordinary variable changes stay inside that capture. The parent still sees its original title afterward. This differs from calling an ordinary function directly, whose non-local assignments can change caller variables.

concepts.title: Files are still shared
concepts.text: An isolated variable environment does not isolate virtual files. The practice helper changes title inside the capture and appends to museum-ledger.txt. The outside title stays original, but the file view shows the new ledger line. Capturing a command is not a way to undo its file writes.

concepts.title: Validate the whole batch before a helper with effects
concepts.text: The assignment helper appends to scan-ledger.txt. Check every source and collision first, including a late missing source, before calling it. Preview preserves the destination, but it deliberately updates this inspection ledger. Failed validation must leave both report and ledger unchanged.

concepts.title: Keep the caller title and the batch decision
concepts.text: Capture the helper body, save its status before printing, and use the original supplied REPORT_TITLE in the wrapper. The helper returns 1 if any source contains BLOCK:, even if the last source is clear. Repeated source arguments remain separate inspections in the original order.

teaching.example:
title='Exhibit review'
make_note() {
    title='Working title'
    printf 'Visited: optics\n' >> museum-ledger.txt
    printf 'Display: ready\n'
}
note=$(make_note)
printf 'Note: <%s>\nOutside: %s\n' "$note" "$title"
teaching.inputs: No arguments or supplied variables. The example creates title and note, defines make_note, and starts with a separate museum ledger. Every practice Run resets that sample file; assignment files/results are independent.
teaching.try_change: Replace note=$(make_note) with make_note; note='direct call' and Run. Compare the outside title and normal output; the ledger effect still happens.

scenarios.retry_guidance: If the title becomes Working scan, distinguish a direct helper call from an isolated capture. If preview changes the report, inspect the publication branch. If a late missing source changes the ledger, finish all validation before inspection.
scenarios.explanation: A called function is inherited by the capture, with a child function-call frame. Its ordinary variable changes do not replace the parent's values. Its writes still affect shared virtual files, so capture is not a filesystem rollback. Full-batch preflight precedes those writes; final files, report text and whole-batch status are checked independently. Any supported equivalent, including a direct reconstruction with no capture, can pass.
